selection_method: Screen existing passenger-terminal and shoreline-corridor feasibility; compare retained census residents and contextual existing ferry endpoint use. Prefer a short direct connection that could remove a transfer. This is not an observed unmet-demand or crowding ranking.

suggestions.title: Hulhumalé ↔ Vilimalé
suggestions.rationale: A short direct link to Vilimalé could bypass a Malé transfer for an island with 6,755 census residents and an existing terminal. Its Malé ferry is already frequent; demand and time savings for this direct route remain unverified.

evidence.title: Maldives Bureau of Statistics: Census 2022, Table P5
evidence.qualification: Combined Vilimaale census wards; excludes the unallocatable multi-island harbour row. Census residents are not current passenger demand. The impact model uses its separately qualified 2026 resident allocation.

evidence.title: Maldives Bureau of Statistics: Maldives in Figures, June 2026, Table 11.2
evidence.value: 226,614 ferry endpoint passenger movements in June 2026; category Villigili (VM Ferry), cell CC162
evidence.qualification: Existing Malé–Vilimalé endpoint category. Repeat travel may be counted. Not unique people, Hulhumalé–Vilimalé demand, occupancy, shortage or a forecast. Opposite endpoint rows must not be added.

evidence.title: MTCC Vilimalé ferry frequency calendar 2026
evidence.value: Published Malé–Vilimalé headway windows: 5–60 minutes; effective 21 March 2026
evidence.qualification: Already frequent existing service. Crossing time is absent; a Saturday 17:20–17:30 interval, expiry and holiday/cancellation exceptions remain unverified. Do not describe Vilimalé as underserved overall.

evidence.title: RTL official vessel route catalogue
evidence.value: Existing Vilimalé terminal rtl:vessel-terminal:3; source snapshot 11 October 2026
evidence.qualification: Official endpoint for MVML, not evidence of arrivals, berth permission or a direct Hulhumalé service.

evidence.title: OpenStreetMap: Hulhumalé Ferry Terminal
evidence.value: Existing mapped origin terminal; no new port construction assumed

qualifications: This is a proposed direct-connection opportunity, not a ranking of highest unmet demand. Observed direct-route demand, queues, occupancy, current capacity and shortage are unknown.
Vilimalé already has frequent Malé ferry service. A direct Hulhumalé link could remove a transfer, but complete timed journeys are unavailable, so total journey minutes saved cannot be claimed.

60-minute headway, 06:00–20:00 hours and 25 km/h speed are editable planning assumptions. The existing model derives the 19-minute crossing, departures, fleet, costs and impacts. They are not optimized service levels or an operator commitment.
Missing retained dated direct service is an evidence gap, not proof that no service operates. Baseline expected-wait savings for a new direct link remain unavailable.
Reusing existing terminals can leave walking-access gains at zero on both islands. Added dated connections and departures are separate benefits; neither establishes ridership.
The modeled corridor avoids mapped shorelines. Depth, reefs, channels, landing access, vessel suitability and permission remain unverified; this is not navigation clearance.

reproduction.cache_basis: Exact full existing operations, complete assumptions including date, reviewed artifact, model code, baseline/calendar/source receipts, all mapped shorelines, marine graph and source terminal catalogue. Changed bus work, dates or inputs calculate a distinct result.
